title: Investigate and patch RTT surge causing first-byte jitter and tokens/sec degradation
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Several enterprise customers (Enterprise-A, BankCorp, HealthSync) reported sudden RTT increases starting 2026-03-09 leading to first-token jitter (TTFT spikes) and tokens/sec degradation across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The surge correlates with a small change in the router affinity heuristic rolled on 2026-03-08 and an accompanying slight shift in kernel selection probability for quantized variants. Impacted workloads include short-chat (few tokens) and low-latency inference endpoints.

Observed symptoms: 
- TTFT increased 2.5–6x for affected sessions; 95th and 99th percentiles most impacted.
- Tokens/sec throughput for bursty sessions dropped ~20–40% depending on model.
- Higher variance when requests cross router shards (cross-affinity sessions).
- Problem reproduces in hosted region us-west-2, dedicated clusters with router-sharding enabled, and Private installations running the new affinity agent.

Investigation notes & telemetry: 
- TokenTracer traces (internal) show extra queuing on router ingress for sessions that lost session-hash affinity (session-hash-drift).
- Kernel chooser logs show increased selection of the fallback int8-kernel for gpt-legacy-v1-quant in cases where the router reported a higher estimated sequence length; this increased per-token processing time for certain micro-batches.
- Dashboard links: 
  - Live SLO board: https://dash.redwood/inference/slo/rtt (internal)
  - TokenTracer sample traces: https://dash.redwood/inference/traces/1726 (internal)

Hypothesis: A change to router affinity heuristic (route-affinity-shim v2) unintentionally increased cross-router session routing during short, bursty traffic patterns. Cross-router handoffs create cold queues and cause the runtime to occasionally pick a safer fallback kernel for quantized variants, compounding latency.

Immediate mitigations applied (2026-03-10 through 2026-03-14):
1) Hot rollback of route-affinity-shim v2 on hosted routers (partial rollback completed 2026-03-11 03:20 UTC).
2) Temporary route policy override for impacted tenants: pin sessions to original router for 30s after session start. Implemented via routing ACL and feature-flag.
3) Emergency tweak to kernel-selection weights: reduce fallback probability for int8 kernels by 40% for short sequences.
4) Turned off speculative multiplexing for affected dedicated clusters to reduce queue variance while we validate other fixes.

Outcomes observed after mitigations: 
- TTFT 95p decreased to within 1.2x baseline for most hosted traffic in us-west-2 within 90 minutes of the rollback.
- Dedicated clusters saw partial improvement; Private installs require additional customer-side config to accept affinity pinning change.

Work remaining / plan: 
- Patch route-affinity-shim to include session-hash-stability checks and a gradual probe window (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/3246). Target for rollout: 2026-03-16 canary.
- Add a router telemetry guardrail that emits high-confidence cross-router handoffs to an alert channel.
- Implement refined kernel-selection probe that logs candidate timings before committing fallback selection; this will help avoid blind fallback decisions under high queue variance.
- Coordinate with Private deployment teams to provide a one-line config toggle and a runbook for affinity pinning.
- Postmortem & customer communications scheduled after stabilization (owner: PM Jenna Ortiz).

Risks and trade-offs: 
- Leaving kernel-weight tweaked too long can expose correctness/perf trade-offs for rare long-sequence workloads; we keep a short TTL on the emergency weight change.
- Affinity pinning increases warm locality but can reduce cross-router load balancing efficacy; we will only enable it for a short probe window and only for tenants with severe impact.

Acceptance criteria for 'Done': 
- TTFT 95p and tokens/sec metrics return to within 10% of baseline across hosted and dedicated after canary.
- Private customers confirm runbook and config applied with improvement.
- Postmortem published and customer-facing incident note drafted.

Links & artifacts: 
- Routing PR (fix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/3246
- Kernel-selection tweak PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1982
- Emergency rollback runbook: https://confluence.redwood/ops/rollbacks/affinity-rollback
- Incident Slack thread (redwood-prod-ops channel): https://slack.com/archives/C12345/p164691 (internal)

Owner: Marco Ruiz (runtime infra). Escalation contact: Jenna Ortiz (PM), ops on-call (primary).
